person.name: Steve_Jobs
person.summary: Steve Jobs was an American entrepreneur, inventor, and investor who co-founded Apple and helped pioneer the personal-computer revolution. After being forced out of Apple in 1985, he founded NeXT and became the controlling owner of Pixar, guiding it to success with computer-animated films. He returned to Apple in 1997 and led a dramatic corporate revival, overseeing landmark products including the iPod and iPhone before stepping down due to illness.

conclusion: Steve Jobs fused engineering, aesthetics, and showmanship into a blueprint for modern consumer technology. His legacy is a world where devices feel personal, storytelling sells the future, and design is treated as destiny.

events.title: Born and adopted
events.description: Steven Paul Jobs was born in San Francisco and was adopted shortly afterward by Paul and Clara Jobs. The adoption was shaped by his biological mother's desire that he be raised by college graduates, later resolved by promises to support his education. Jobs grew up identifying strongly with his adoptive parents as his family.

events.title: Moved to Los Altos
events.description: Jobs’s family relocated within the [[San Francisco Bay Area|San Francisco Bay Area]], allowing him to attend schools tied closely to [[Silicon Valley|Silicon Valley]]’s emerging electronics culture. Around this period, his interest in building and tinkering was encouraged at home, especially through time spent with his father in the garage. The move placed him near future collaborators and formative opportunities.

San Francisco Bay Area.explanation: A populous Northern California region centered on San Francisco Bay, encompassing cities such as San Francisco, San Jose, and nearby suburbs where Jobs grew up.

Silicon Valley.explanation: A region in the southern Bay Area known for its concentration of high-technology companies and engineering culture, influential in Jobs’s early interests.

events.title: Attended and left Reed
events.description: Jobs enrolled at [[Reed College|Reed College]] in [[Portland, Oregon|Oregon]] but soon withdrew after one semester, concerned about the cost and direction of his education. He remained connected by auditing classes, including calligraphy, which later influenced Apple’s emphasis on typography and design. The experience reinforced his preference for self-directed learning and unconventional paths.

images.caption: Steve Jobs in Homestead High School yearbook (1972)
images.creator: Homestead High School

Reed College.explanation: A private liberal-arts college in Portland, Oregon, known for an unconventional academic culture; Jobs attended briefly in 1972 and later audited classes there.

Portland, Oregon.explanation: The largest city in Oregon and the location of Reed College, where Jobs enrolled and later audited classes after withdrawing.

events.date_note: Dates are approximate; the period includes his work at Atari and his travel in India
events.title: Atari work and India trip
events.description: In 1974, Jobs worked at [[Atari, Inc.|Atari]], gaining exposure to fast-paced product development and the commercial side of electronics, while maintaining close ties with Steve Wozniak. During this era he also traveled through India seeking spiritual insight and later deepened his interest in Zen Buddhism. These experiences shaped both his personal discipline and his later leadership style.

Atari, Inc..explanation: Early video game and arcade game company (founded 1972) where Jobs worked as a technician, gaining experience in shipping consumer electronics products.

events.title: Co-founded Apple
events.description: Jobs and Steve Wozniak co-founded Apple Computer to develop and sell the Apple I and pursue a new kind of personal computing business. Jobs pushed for a product that could be manufactured and marketed beyond hobbyist circles, helping turn Wozniak’s designs into a company. Apple quickly became a focal point of the emerging microcomputer industry.

events.title: Apple II and IPO boom
events.description: With the Apple II, Apple achieved mass-market success and helped define the personal-computer boom. Jobs became a public face of a new technology industry, combining product vision with sharp marketing instincts. Apple’s rapid growth culminated in its 1980 [[initial public offering|initial public offering]], making Jobs a multimillionaire and cementing Apple as a major company.

locations.name_modern: New York City, New York, United States

initial public offering.explanation: A company’s first sale of shares to the public on a stock exchange, used to raise capital and establish a public market valuation.

events.title: Pursued GUI after Xerox
events.description: After seeing the [[Xerox Alto|Xerox Alto’s]] [[graphical user interface|graphical user interface]] and mouse-driven approach at Xerox PARC in 1979, Jobs pushed Apple toward more human-friendly computing. This insight drove work that produced the Apple Lisa and, more importantly, set the direction for the Macintosh. The episode showed Jobs’s knack for recognizing transformative ideas and demanding their commercialization.

images.caption: Entrance to Xerox PARC in Palo Alto, California
images.creator: Coolcaesar at English Wikipedia

Xerox Alto.explanation: A pioneering Xerox research computer (early 1970s) whose bitmapped display, windows, icons, and mouse interaction strongly influenced later personal computer interfaces.

graphical user interface.explanation: An interface style that lets users interact through on-screen visual elements (windows, icons, menus, pointer) rather than typing only text commands.

events.title: Launched Macintosh platform
events.description: Jobs led the high-profile launch of the Macintosh, bringing a mass-produced GUI computer to a wide audience. The platform helped spark [[desktop publishing|desktop publishing]] when paired with tools like Apple’s LaserWriter and software such as [[Aldus PageMaker|Aldus PageMaker]]. Although early sales pressures mounted, the Macintosh became central to Apple’s identity and Jobs’s legacy as a product evangelist.

images.caption: Steve Jobs with Macintosh computer, January 1984
images.creator: Photo: Bernard Gotfryd - Edited from tif by Cart

desktop publishing.explanation: The use of personal computers, page-layout software, and laser printers to design and produce print-ready documents, a publishing workflow that expanded rapidly in the mid-1980s.

Aldus PageMaker.explanation: An early, influential page-layout program (first released in 1985) that, together with the Macintosh and LaserWriter, helped popularize desktop publishing.

events.title: Left Apple amid power struggle
events.description: A prolonged conflict with Apple’s board and CEO John Sculley ended with Jobs losing managerial power and departing the company he co-founded. The break was a defining professional setback that forced him to rebuild outside Apple. It also set the stage for his later return under dramatically different circumstances.

events.title: Founded NeXT
events.description: Jobs founded NeXT, bringing a group of former Apple colleagues to build advanced computers for higher-education and business markets. He positioned NeXT as a high-end platform company, emphasizing software and design alongside hardware. NeXT’s technology later became crucial to Apple’s software future.

events.date_note: End date reflects the release period of Toy Story, Pixar’s first feature film
events.title: Built Pixar into studio
events.description: Jobs bought Lucasfilm’s [[Graphics Group|computer graphics division]] and created Pixar, becoming its chairman and controlling owner. Over years of investment and organizational pressure, Pixar transitioned from a technology venture into a film studio. The release of Toy Story validated the model of feature-length computer animation and established Pixar as a major creative force.

images.caption: Entrance to Pixar's studio lot in Emeryville, California
images.creator: P.gobin at English Wikipedia

Graphics Group.explanation: The Computer Division subgroup at Lucasfilm that developed early computer-graphics and animation technology; Steve Jobs bought it in 1986 and it became the core of Pixar.

events.title: Returned to rescue Apple
events.description: After Apple acquired NeXT, Jobs returned to Apple and soon took the CEO role, confronting a company widely seen as near collapse. He reorganized product strategy and branding, including the high-visibility "Think different" campaign. The turnaround accelerated with products like the iMac, developed in close collaboration with designer Jony Ive.

events.title: Created Apple’s digital ecosystem
events.description: Jobs pushed Apple beyond computers by building an integrated hardware-and-services strategy, expanding Apple’s consumer reach. During this period Apple opened retail stores, introduced the iPod, and developed iTunes into a broader platform. The approach strengthened Apple’s financial recovery and redefined the company around end-to-end product experiences.

images.caption: Steve Jobs demonstrates the MacBook Air at Macworld 2008
images.creator: Aljawad

events.title: Cancer diagnosis
events.description: Jobs was diagnosed with a [[pancreatic neuroendocrine tumor|pancreatic neuroendocrine tumor]], a serious illness that increasingly affected his public role and internal succession planning. Despite treatment and intermittent absences, he continued to shape major product decisions. His health became a recurring factor in Apple’s leadership transitions during the final decade of his life.

pancreatic neuroendocrine tumor.explanation: A relatively rare type of pancreatic tumor arising from hormone-producing (neuroendocrine) cells; it often behaves differently from the more common pancreatic adenocarcinoma.

events.title: Unveiled the iPhone
events.description: Jobs introduced the iPhone, presenting it as a convergence of phone, iPod, and internet device and repositioning Apple as a dominant force in mobile computing. The launch helped catalyze the modern smartphone era and expanded Apple’s influence far beyond the PC market. It also reinforced Jobs’s reputation for product storytelling and platform building.

images.caption: Steve Jobs during his keynote at Macworld Expo 2007
images.creator: JD Lasica from Pleasanton, CA, US

events.title: Resigned as Apple CEO
events.description: Jobs resigned as Apple’s chief executive amid declining health and helped formalize the leadership transition to Tim Cook. He remained involved as chairman, preserving continuity while reducing day-to-day responsibilities. The change marked the end of his active tenure running Apple’s operations.

events.title: Died in 2011
events.description: Jobs died from complications related to his [[pancreatic neuroendocrine tumor|pancreatic neuroendocrine tumor]]. His death closed a career that spanned the personal-computer revolution, the rise of modern digital consumer electronics, and the mainstreaming of computer animation through Pixar. In his final years he remained closely associated with Apple’s product direction even as health limited his public presence.

pancreatic neuroendocrine tumor.explanation: A relatively rare pancreatic tumor arising from hormone-producing (neuroendocrine) cells; it often differs in behavior and treatment from the more common pancreatic adenocarcinoma.
